title: Primary Function of the System
learningObjectives: Identify the primary function of an industrial line-shaft system.
student: What is the primary mechanical function of the line-shaft system?
instructor: The shaft supports mounted pulleys and transfers rotational power between the driving and driven equipment.

title: External Transverse Loading
learningObjectives: Recognize the transverse loading produced by belt drives.
student: Besides transmitting torque, what type of loading do the belt drives apply to the shaft?
instructor: The belts apply transverse forces to the pulleys. Those pulley forces are transferred into the shaft and create bending.

title: Supports
learningObjectives: Explain the mechanical role of shaft bearings.
student: What is the mechanical role of the shaft bearings?
instructor: The bearings support and align the rotating shaft, transfer transverse shaft loads into the machine structure, and allow the shaft to rotate.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace transverse force transfer through the system.
student: Trace the transverse load path from a belt to the machine foundation.
instructor: Belt → pulley/sheave → shaft → bearings → machine frame / equipment foundation.

title: Effect of an Overhung Pulley
learningObjectives: Explain why an overhung pulley affects shaft bending.
student: Why can a pulley mounted outside a bearing be important when evaluating shaft bending?
instructor: An overhung pulley applies its transverse force beyond the bearing location. This creates an additional moment arm and can substantially influence the nearby shaft bending and the bearing reactions.

title: Relevant Mechanical Response
learningObjectives: Select the internal responses needed to identify the critical bending location.
student: What internal mechanical responses are needed to identify the portion of the shaft most highly loaded in bending?
instructor: The vertical shear-force and bending-moment distributions are required. The shaft location with the largest absolute bending moment is the first location to examine in a later bending-stress analysis.

title: Relevant Layout Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify the layout parameters controlling the bending-moment distribution.
student: What physical characteristics of the shaft layout influence the bending-moment distribution?
instructor: The important characteristics are the magnitudes and directions of the pulley forces, the locations of the pulleys, the bearing locations, and any overhung distances.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
learningObjectives: Convert the physical line shaft into a one-dimensional beam model.
student: Convert the real line-shaft system into a one-dimensional beam model that preserves the dominant transverse load path. Show the two bearing supports, the pulley-force resultants, and the overhung pulley.
instructor: A correct model represents the shaft as a slender beam supported by two bearings, with concentrated transverse forces applied at the pulley centers and one pulley located beyond the right bearing.
gradingNotes: The physical system should be interpreted first. Detailed symbols and segment labels are introduced only in the instructor reference model.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State the assumptions defining the simplified beam model.
student: State the assumptions used to convert the rotating shaft assembly into the simplified beam model.
instructor: Static transverse loading; shaft modeled as a slender beam; each pulley/belt action replaced by a concentrated vertical resultant at the pulley center; bearings provide vertical reactions only in the selected analysis plane; shaft self-weight is neglected; deformation is small; torsion, axial loading, dynamic belt effects, bearing friction, and local hub/contact stresses are excluded.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
learningObjectives: Plan the reaction and internal-resultant analysis.
student: Describe the analysis sequence before numerical calculations are performed.
instructor: Use equilibrium of the complete shaft to determine the bearing reactions, move along the shaft to construct the shear-force diagram, obtain the bending-moment diagram from the shear distribution, write piecewise internal-resultant functions, identify the absolute maximum bending moment, and make a limited layout recommendation.

title: Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: State the bearing idealizations at A and B.
student: From the instructor model, state the bearing idealizations at A and B.
instructor: Bearings A and B provide vertical reactions in the selected 2D analysis plane. They allow shaft rotation and do not provide reaction moments.

title: Unknown Constraint Loads
instructor: The unknown reactions are Ay and By, taken positive upward.

title: Solve for Bearing Reactions
learningObjectives: Calculate both bearing reactions from whole-shaft equilibrium.
student: Use equilibrium of the entire shaft to determine Ay and By. Write the symbolic equations before numerical substitution.

title: Shear-Force Diagram
learningObjectives: Construct and label the complete vertical shear-force diagram.
student: Construct the vertical shear-force diagram from bearing A to the overhung end and label the shear in each constant-shear region.
instructor: A to pulley 1: V = {{line_V1_N}} N. After pulley 1: V = {{line_V2_N}} N. After pulley 2: V = {{line_V3_N}} N. After bearing B: V = {{line_V4_N}} N. After pulley 3: V = {{line_V5_N}} N.

title: Bending-Moment Diagram
learningObjectives: Construct the bending-moment diagram and calculate its station ordinates.
student: Construct the bending-moment diagram and report the moment at each load and bearing station.
instructor: M(A) = {{line_MA_Nm}} N·m. At pulley 1, M = {{line_M1_Nm}} N·m. At pulley 2, M = {{line_M2_Nm}} N·m. At bearing B, M = {{line_MB_Nm}} N·m. At the overhung free end, M = {{line_M3_Nm}} N·m.

title: Piecewise Internal Resultants
learningObjectives: Write piecewise shear and bending-moment functions.
student: Write V(x) and M(x) piecewise using x measured from bearing A and a consistent sign convention.

title: Absolute Maximum Bending Moment
learningObjectives: Locate and quantify the absolute maximum bending moment.
student: Determine the absolute maximum bending moment and identify its location.
instructor: The largest magnitude is |M|max = {{line_Mmax_abs_Nm}} N·m at the {{line_Mmax_station}}, x = {{line_Mmax_x_mm}} mm from bearing A.

title: Engineering Assessment and Recommendation
learningObjectives: Connect the governing moment to a later strength check and a defensible layout recommendation.
student: Which shaft station should be checked first in a later bending-stress calculation? Identify one layout change that could reduce bending demand and explain why the full diagram must be recomputed after the change.
